protocol.question: For both signs of the fluid velocity, what changes when the whole marker cloud is reflected, and when local neighboring geometry is reflected around fixed centers?
protocol.reuse: Nine verified t=.3 full fluid checkpoints and original/reversed trajectories from ../velocity-reversal; no reconstruction of initial conditions, no original long-matrix runs, no refitting predictors.
protocol.reflection: R=diag(-1,1,1), mirror about the x=0 plane in the periodic box of side 6.
protocol.four_global_cells: Original positions x and reflected positions Rx, each integrated in +u and -u. The entire Eulerian field is held in its original spatial frame. Global reflection preserves neighbor distances/angles but changes sampling locations; it does not isolate orientation from location.
protocol.anchored_geometry: At every original central marker, take its original eight kNN offsets r. Construct virtual passive neighbors at x+Rr while retaining the same center x. Integrate these neighbors in the same fluid branch. Compare with original neighbors traced by their original indices. This preserves center, initial distances and all neighbor angles, while reflecting the local arrangement relative to an unchanged fluid field. Virtual neighbor sets are independent overlapping diagnostic probes, not a single material packing.
protocol.targets: Global clouds: infinitesimal numerical forward FTLE, log sigma_max(tangent)/horizon. Anchored neighborhoods: regularized least-squares finite-cloud deformation, log sigma_max(F_cloud)/horizon, plus average log change of pair distances. These are finite-neighborhood diagnostics, not interchangeable with infinitesimal FTLE.
protocol.events: Original training-only FTLE cutoff, unchanged and applied only to the .2 infinitesimal target; no event cutoff is assigned to the distinct finite-cloud metric.
protocol.comparisons: Four-cell same-label differences/correlations and fixed-threshold event Jaccard/disagreement. Anchored finite-cloud arrangement contrast averaged over direction, direction contrast averaged over arrangement, and difference-in-differences interaction. No claims that contrasts partition variance uniquely or prove a marker force.
protocol.symmetry_control: On the first pilot only (seed1024 grid38), also reflect the complete Eulerian vector field u_m(x)=R u(Rx) and globally reflected markers. Integrate both velocity signs. Require full trajectories/tangents/targets to agree with consistently reflected original branches within 1e-9. A consistent whole-state mirror is a symmetry control, not an arrangement-only intervention.
protocol.checks: Pilot first. Verify reused NPZ and checkpoint hashes, identical-center original trajectories against archived branches, original gradients/tangents, neighbor radii/angles, same-label symmetry targets, finite states, CFL<.5, relative energy residual<.005, spectral divergence<1e-10. Preserve failures and do not expand automatically.
protocol.scope: Nine short joint integrations, each with two velocity signs and original/global-mirror/anchored-neighbor probes; one additional two-sign full-state mirror symmetry control. Existing original/reversed outcomes are reused as checks. Four independent initial conditions, two dependent spatial grids and one half-step control. No spatial convergence claim.
protocol.interpretation: Point-marker rearrangement cannot change the Eulerian flow or infinitesimal target at a fixed starting center in this passive model. Moving markers can change which high-strain regions they sample. Finite-cloud deformation can depend on relative geometry. Neither physical material memory nor a particular arrangement's causal influence on flow is established.
